llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed local Word comment extractor with some ordinary security hardening gaps, but no evidence of hidden access, exfiltration, persistence, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The skill is Windows- and Microsoft Word-specific, which fits the advertised page-number feature; the script extracts the full DOCX archive without size limits, so untrusted or malformed documents could cause local resource exhaustion.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation asks the user to run an unpinned pip install for pywin32, which is a mutable dependency boundary but is a normal dependency for disclosed Word COM automation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to a user-provided DOCX path and formatting the extracted comments; the Word COM use for page numbers is disclosed in the manifest and notes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No startup hooks, scheduled tasks, memory writes, credential handling, privilege escalation, tool wrapping, or cross-session persistence were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is extracting Word comments, anchor text, and page numbers, then asking the agent to polish review comments; the Python script and instructions align with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only in an isolated Python environment, pin pywin32 if possible, and avoid running the extractor on DOCX files from untrusted sources until archive size and member validation are added.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] expected: The script launches Microsoft Word through COM to retrieve comment page numbers; this is broader than pure parsing but is clearly disclosed as required for the page-number feature.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese keywords reflect the likely workflow audience and discovery terms; they do not introduce hidden authority or unsafe behavior.
[T09] unexpected: The script uses ZipFile.extractall on a user-supplied DOCX without explicit member or size limits, which is a real local denial-of-service hardening gap but not evidence of malicious intent.
[T08] expected: The unpinned pywin32 install is supply-chain mutable and should be pinned, but the dependency itself is purpose-aligned and disclosed.
